classifications.goal_a: Connect a Node.js API service to a MongoDB service, both running under docker-compose
classifications.blocker_a: Connection refused when using the mongo hostname/credentials in the connection string despite compose networking being set up; likely auth/connection string or network configuration issue between compose services
classifications.goal_b: Run a Node.js server and a MongoDB instance together inside a single container/image
classifications.blocker_b: The apt package name 'mongodb' has no installation candidate on the base image, so the Dockerfile build fails before the container can even be assembled
classifications.brief_rationale: Person A already has both services running as separate compose containers and is blocked by a runtime network/connection-string issue between them; person B is blocked earlier, at build time, because the package needed to co-install MongoDB inside a single image cannot be found. Both involve Node.js and MongoDB in Docker, but the blocked goals -- inter-service connectivity versus package installability for a single-container setup -- require different interventions.

classifications.goal_a: Deploy a Spring Boot Java app to Render using a Docker container
classifications.blocker_a: The jar file appears corrupt/invalid when run in the container, possibly related to file size or build/upload issues
classifications.goal_b: Deploy an Angular application to OpenShift via a GitLab-based container workflow
classifications.blocker_b: No specific failure is described; the person is asking for general step-by-step guidance on the deployment workflow, not reporting a blockage
classifications.brief_rationale: Person A has a concrete blocked goal (corrupt jarfile preventing app run on Render), but person B's question is a request for general deployment guidance with no stated failure or blockage. Since B's goal/blocker is not established as a problem, no meaningful comparison of blocked goals can be made.

classifications.goal_a: Persist Postgres data/migrations across docker-compose restarts
classifications.blocker_a: Using an external named volume with docker-compose down/up, data appears lost and migrations must be rerun
classifications.goal_b: Have an init SQL script create a schema and table inside a Postgres container on startup
classifications.blocker_b: The docker-entrypoint-initdb.d script runs but the schema/table are not created, only the database appears
classifications.brief_rationale: A is about data/state not persisting across container restarts due to volume/lifecycle handling, while B is about an initialization SQL script not producing the expected schema/table on first run. These are different blocked goals -- persistence across runs vs. correct execution of init scripts -- even though both involve Postgres in Docker.

classifications.goal_a: Pass a command-line port argument to a Flask app so a shell script argument reaches the running container's process.
classifications.blocker_a: The run script/CMD in the Dockerfile isn't actually passing sys.argv[1] to userapi.py, so app_port is never set and raises ValueError.
classifications.goal_b: Set up an automated deployment/update workflow for a continuously running python script on a remote Raspberry Pi.
classifications.blocker_b: Unsure how to orchestrate pulling git updates, stopping and restarting the script automatically without manual intervention.
classifications.brief_rationale: Person A is blocked by a command-line argument not being passed through to a script inside a Docker container, while Person B is trying to design a remote deployment/update workflow for a persistent script. These are different blocked goals -- argument propagation versus deployment automation -- with no single intervention addressing both.

classifications.goal_a: Get a Python script using pyjwt/oauthlib RSA signing to run correctly inside a Docker container
classifications.blocker_a: Inside the Docker image, jwt.algorithms lacks the 'hashes' attribute, causing an AttributeError, despite matching package versions locally
classifications.goal_b: Get a Flask API running in Docker to start listening on a dynamically specified port passed at runtime
classifications.blocker_b: The startup script/CMD does not actually pass the port argument through to the Python script, so sys.argv is empty and the app raises a ValueError
classifications.brief_rationale: Person A is blocked by a dependency/version conflict causing an AttributeError in a JWT/OAuth library inside Docker, while Person B is blocked by a shell/CMD argument-passing issue preventing a port number from reaching their Flask script. These are different blocked goals (library compatibility vs. argument propagation) with no single shared intervention.

classifications.goal_a: Get a Next.js env variable to have a value at runtime in a Kubernetes-deployed app
classifications.blocker_a: NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are inlined at build time, so values set only in the k8s ConfigMap at runtime never reach the compiled app
classifications.goal_b: Get the psycopg PostgreSQL Python library to install successfully in a Docker image build
classifications.blocker_b: pip install of psycopg fails on Alpine because required build toolchain/native dependencies for compiling it are missing
classifications.brief_rationale: Person A is blocked by a build-time/run-time lifecycle mismatch for env variables, while person B is blocked by missing native build dependencies needed to compile a Python package on Alpine. These are different blocked goals with unrelated interventions (documentation about variable injection timing vs. adding OS packages for compilation).

classifications.goal_a: Get the psycopg Python library to build/install successfully inside an Alpine-based Docker image
classifications.blocker_a: pip install fails with exit code 1 because required build dependencies for compiling psycopg on musl/Alpine are missing
classifications.goal_b: Mount multiple distinct Docker volumes into the same target path inside one container
classifications.blocker_b: Docker daemon rejects the run command with 'Duplicate mount point' since two -v flags specify the same target directory
classifications.brief_rationale: A is about getting a Python package to compile in an Alpine image due to missing build toolchain dependencies, while B is about Docker's volume mount semantics preventing two volumes from sharing one target path. These are unrelated blocked goals with no single intervention addressing both.

classifications.goal_a: Share a single built DLL artifact across multiple Docker image builds instead of rebuilding it per project
classifications.blocker_a: Each Dockerfile independently builds the shared dependency, with no known mechanism to build once and reuse across images
classifications.goal_b: Have Docker Compose services (in host network mode) communicate using a specific host network interface rather than the default one
classifications.blocker_b: Docker defaults to using the ens0 interface's IP, and there's no known way to direct it to use ens192 instead
classifications.brief_rationale: Person A wants to avoid duplicate builds of a shared artifact across Dockerfiles, while person B wants to control which host network interface Docker/Compose binds to. These are unrelated blocked goals (build artifact sharing vs. network interface selection) with no single intervention addressing both.

classifications.goal_a: Use an environment variable to name a network in the top-level `networks:` section of a compose/stack file
classifications.blocker_a: `docker stack config` does not substitute `${network}` when used as a key under the root `networks:` section, though it works when used as a value under a service's `networks:` list
classifications.goal_b: Get a Go CLI application container to successfully connect to a Postgres database container via Docker Compose
classifications.blocker_b: Running the app container standalone with `docker run` (bypassing compose networking) and using `localhost` as the DB host causes connection refused, since the containers aren't on the same compose network/service-name resolution isn't used
classifications.brief_rationale: A is blocked by Compose/stack variable-substitution not applying to YAML map keys in the top-level networks section, a templating/interpolation limitation. B is blocked by inter-container network reachability (using localhost instead of the compose service name) between a Go app and Postgres. These are different blocked goals with different interventions -- one is about docker-compose variable interpolation semantics, the other about container networking configuration.

classifications.goal_a: Define a Docker Compose/stack network name dynamically using an environment variable at the top-level networks key.
classifications.blocker_a: Docker stack config does not interpolate environment variables when used as YAML keys under the root "networks" section.
classifications.goal_b: Keep a Hawkbit server with MySQL backend running reliably long-term via docker-compose.
classifications.blocker_b: MySQL data/volume appears to be lost after a few hours, causing "Unknown database" errors, seemingly due to a volume misconfiguration.
classifications.brief_rationale: Person A is blocked by Compose/stack variable interpolation not applying to YAML keys in the networks section, while person B is blocked by persistent volume/data loss causing database connectivity failure after uptime. These are different blocked goals -- one about environment variable substitution scope, the other about data persistence -- and no single intervention addresses both.

classifications.goal_a: Get a Dockerized JupyterLab app (installed via pipenv) to start via docker compose
classifications.blocker_a: Container fails: exec "/app/.venv/bin/pipenv": stat ... no such file or directory -- pipenv virtualenv binary not present at expected path, likely because host bind mount overwrote /app and hid the built venv
classifications.goal_b: Get a FastAPI app to run under gunicorn managing uvicorn workers inside a Docker container
classifications.blocker_b: Container fails: exec "gunicorn": executable file not found in $PATH -- gunicorn was installed only in the builder stage, not copied/available in runtime stage's venv/PATH
classifications.brief_rationale: Both show the same "OCI runtime create failed ... executable file not found/no such file" daemon wrapper text, but A's issue is a missing venv binary likely due to a volume mount overwriting /app, while B's issue is a missing binary because it wasn't installed/copied into the runtime stage's environment -- different blocked goals needing different interventions (fixing bind-mount/build artifact placement vs. fixing multistage dependency copying).

classifications.goal_a: Run Django migrations against Postgres during the Docker image build, inside a single container
classifications.blocker_a: Postgres server wasn't actually running/listening on localhost at the RUN step when migrate was invoked, causing connection refused
classifications.goal_b: Have a PHP app inside one container reach another service (InfluxDB) over the Docker Compose network
classifications.blocker_b: Used 'localhost' which refers to the app container itself rather than the target service's container, so the service name/network alias was needed instead
classifications.brief_rationale: A is about a service not yet being started/available within a single-container build step, while B is about cross-container network addressing (localhost vs service name) in multi-container Compose; these require different interventions (process lifecycle vs. Docker networking/DNS).

classifications.goal_a: Get a Docker container's entrypoint script to run so the app starts successfully.
classifications.blocker_a: The copied entrypoint.sh lacks execute permission, causing "permission denied" when the container tries to run it.
classifications.goal_b: Run both a Node.js server and a MongoDB instance together inside a single Docker container.
classifications.blocker_b: The apt package name 'mongodb' is not available in the base image's package repository, so the build fails to install it.
classifications.brief_rationale: A is blocked by a file-permission issue preventing an entrypoint script from executing, while B is blocked by an unavailable apt package needed to co-locate two services in one container. These are different blocked goals despite both being Docker build/run failures.

classifications.goal_a: Reliably read an env var value from inside a running container, regardless of shell/session context
classifications.blocker_a: Confused by shell/session-dependent behavior: variable visible in poetry-activated exec session but not in plain exec session, unclear why container output differs by invocation context
classifications.goal_b: Get GitHub Actions workflow env variables (non-secret) propagated into a docker-compose managed container running on a remote server
classifications.blocker_b: GitHub Actions `env.*` variables are not substituted/exported into the SSH script the way `secrets.*` are, so docker-compose's `${VAR}` substitution doesn't pick them up
classifications.brief_rationale: A is puzzled by inconsistent shell-session visibility of an already-injected env var inside a running container, while B is trying to propagate CI workflow variables through SSH/export into docker-compose's variable substitution at build/deploy time. These are different blocked goals (session/shell scoping confusion vs. cross-system variable propagation from CI to compose), so no single intervention addresses both beyond the generic 'docker env vars' category.

classifications.goal_a: Get a multistage Docker build to produce a working netCDF4 install with full native performance carried over from the compile stage
classifications.blocker_a: Copying the venv (with netCDF4/h5py) into the final stage causes a large slowdown in netCDF read/write, suspected missing/incorrectly linked native C libraries
classifications.goal_b: Get a Rails app's Docker build to install system packages so Node/Ruby toolchain setup succeeds
classifications.blocker_b: apt-get install of libc-bin segfaults under emulated arm64 (qemu), causing dpkg post-install script to fail and the build to abort
classifications.brief_rationale: A is about a native library losing correct linkage/performance when copied between multistage build stages, while B is about a package's post-install script segfaulting under QEMU emulation during a single apt-get step. These are different blocked goals (runtime library linkage/performance vs. architecture-emulation package installation failure) that no single intervention would address.

classifications.goal_a: Manage/join a pre-existing external Docker network from Terraform-provisioned containers
classifications.blocker_a: Terraform docker provider has no clear way to mark/reference a network as 'external' like docker-compose does; labels attempt didn't work
classifications.goal_b: Have Docker Compose services using host network mode communicate over a specific network interface
classifications.blocker_b: Docker defaults to using one NIC (ens0) and there's no apparent way to direct it to bind/use a different interface (ens192)
classifications.brief_rationale: A is about referencing/creating an externally-managed Docker network via Terraform tooling, while B is about selecting which host network interface a host-mode container uses; these are different blocked goals despite both being 'docker networking' issues.
